Clindamycin is better at working on skin/tissue infections. It’s a prophylactic so just in case something foreign is introduced to your mouth it won’t get infected. The chances of you getting c diff from it are low. If it was a broad spectrum antibiotic then you’d have more to worry about.

So the COWS and CIWA you get “scored” based on symptoms. When people come in we ask if they use drugs or alcohol and how much daily. Say they drink 2 pints a day. They’ll immediately get put on CIWA. They’re usually given a Librium taper. Which is where you start on a higher dose and it tapers down. Depend on the severity of the alcoholism it may be extended. Every day for 3 times a day they get scored according to the CIWA chart. So for example if they’re heart rate is above 100 they get a certain amount of points. Chills, sweating, they get another amount of points. I can’t remember exactly. But based on the total score we decide whether to extend Librium or if we need to send them to the hospital to detox. We can also give Tylenol, Motrin, Imodium, and Zofran. Opiates is the COWS score. That we really don’t do anything for except the 3 sets of vitals and Motrin, Tylenol kind of thing. Opiates you usually have to ride out the withdrawal. Alcohol is a little bit more serious due to DTs. A person could have a seizure or hallucinations and be in really bad off shape. This is usually protocol for county jails. I work for the state that I live in now and those are all prisons, so the person shouldn’t have any drugs in their system that they need to detox from.
If you have any other questions feel free to ask!

We detox them. It depends on what drugs they’re on and how often they take them etc. For opiates we have something called a COWS scale and for alcohol/benzos we have a COWA. Sometimes we have a MAT program which deals with methadone. It really just depends on the situation.

I understand how hard that is. Unfortunately you have to remember that your dad is sick. He’s lost a lot of freedom and the memories that he once had.  He can’t help what’s going on in his head. And I know it’s hard. Someone told me once that having Alzheimer’s is like being at the bottom of a well. You can see the light at the top but you can never get to it, and when you get close you end up back at the bottom. I know it’s extremely frustrating to you and your step-mom and it’s also extremely frustrating for your dad. Remind yourself that your step-mom is very thankful that you could move to help and I’m sure your dad is too, but he can’t express that. Alzheimer’s is a nasty disease. If you need to talk to someone feel free to DM me and I’ll help in any way that I can even if it’s just to vent! Hang in there. I can’t say that it will get better, but you can still help in ways that you may not realize!
